name: awesome-reverse-engineering
desc: Curated reverse-engineering tools and learning resources for binaries, apps, firmware, formats, and protocols.

resources.name: Azeria Labs
resources.desc: ARM assembly tutorials with exercises for learning registers, memory, and calling conventions.

resources.name: Compiler Explorer
resources.desc: Compiles code in the browser with many compilers and shows the generated assembly, for seeing how source constructs and optimization levels translate to machine code.

resources.name: Corkami
resources.desc: Visual references and posters explaining binary formats and file structures, including executable-format layouts.

resources.name: Corkami PoCs
resources.desc: Minimal and unusual executable and document samples for studying file-format edge cases and parser behavior.

resources.name: Hextree
resources.desc: Hands-on mobile and hardware reverse-engineering courses and interactive labs; Commercial, with some free content.

resources.name: Malware Analysis Training
resources.desc: Windows malware-analysis course with programming, Windows-internals, and reversing exercises; labs need a suitable Windows analysis environment.

resources.name: Malware Unicorn RE101
resources.desc: Introductory Windows malware-reversing workshop covering x86 assembly, triage, and debugging; its VM-based lab instructions use older software images.

resources.name: Nightmare
resources.desc: Course built from annotated CTF challenges, progressing from assembly and reversing basics to binary exploitation.

resources.name: OpenSecurityTraining2
resources.desc: Structured courses in assembly, architecture, debugging, and reverse engineering.

resources.name: pwn.college
resources.desc: Free courses with hands-on challenges in Linux, assembly, reverse engineering, and binary exploitation, run in a browser-accessible environment.

resources.name: Reverse Engineering by Kevin Thomas
resources.desc: Annotated assembly and reverse-engineering lessons across x86, x64, ARM, AVR, and RISC-V, with lesson-specific toolchain and hardware requirements.

resources.name: Reverse Engineering for Beginners
resources.desc: Free book connecting compiled C and C++ examples to assembly across several architectures.

resources.name: RPISEC Modern Binary Exploitation
resources.desc: Course materials and labs covering reverse engineering, memory corruption, and exploitation; no commits since December 2021, so labs may need older toolchains.

resources.name: Hacking the Xbox
resources.desc: Introduction to hardware reverse engineering through the original Xbox's security design; free PDF edition released by the author.

resources.name: Practical Binary Analysis
resources.desc: Covers ELF and PE internals, disassembly, binary instrumentation, taint analysis, and symbolic execution, with tools built in the exercises.

resources.name: Practical Malware Analysis
resources.desc: Hands-on introduction to static and dynamic Windows malware analysis with lab exercises; published in 2012, so some tooling chapters are dated.

resources.name: The Ghidra Book
resources.desc: Guide to Ghidra's disassembler, decompiler, scripting, and extension APIs; the 2026 second edition covers BSim and PyGhidra.

resources.name: capa
resources.desc: Identifies capabilities in executable files using rules over static or dynamic analysis results.

resources.name: checksec
resources.desc: Checks ELF security properties such as PIE, RELRO, stack canaries, and non-executable stacks; mitigation flags are not a vulnerability verdict.

resources.name: Detect It Easy
resources.desc: Identifies executable formats, compilers, packers, and other file characteristics.

resources.name: FLOSS
resources.desc: Recovers obfuscated strings, including strings constructed on the stack.

resources.name: hexvero
resources.desc: Statically triages Electron archives and JavaScript bundles for IPC channels, preload bridges, and window settings, plus ELF/Mach-O/PE imports and hardening; its CLI, MCP server, and local web UI require Node.js 22.12+, and pattern-based JavaScript analysis can miss indirect code.

resources.name: LIEF
resources.desc: Parses and modifies executable formats such as PE, ELF, and Mach-O from code.

resources.name: Malcat
resources.desc: Hex editor and disassembler for triaging unknown files, with 50+ format parsers, embedded-file extraction, YARA scanning, and Python scripting. Commercial, with a free Lite edition for non-professional use.

resources.name: PE-bear
resources.desc: Graphical PE viewer and editor for a quick first look at headers, sections, imports, and resources, including malformed files.

resources.name: pestudio
resources.desc: Flags suspicious imports, strings, resources, and other indicators in Windows executables for initial assessment. Commercial, with a free basic edition for private use.

resources.name: Binary Ninja
resources.desc: Interactive disassembler and decompiler with intermediate representations and scripting APIs. Commercial, with a free edition.

resources.name: Cutter
resources.desc: Graphical reverse-engineering interface built on Rizin.

resources.name: Decompiler Explorer
resources.desc: Web service that runs an uploaded binary through several decompilers and shows their output side by side.

resources.name: Ghidra
resources.desc: Disassembly, decompilation, scripting, and headless analysis for native binaries.

resources.name: IDA
resources.desc: Interactive disassembler and decompiler with processor modules and a plugin ecosystem. Commercial, with a free edition.

resources.name: radare2
resources.desc: Command-line toolkit for disassembly, binary inspection, debugging, and scripting.

resources.name: REDasm
resources.desc: Native disassembler and analysis GUI with legacy-format support; Windows and Linux are the primary tested hosts, while other platform builds have lower support tiers.

resources.name: RetDec
resources.desc: Retargetable LLVM-based decompiler for ELF, PE, Mach-O, and other formats; in limited maintenance mode, with little new development.

resources.name: rev.ng
resources.desc: LLVM- and QEMU-based binary-analysis framework and decompiler for inspecting and transforming native code; source builds need its documented toolchain.

resources.name: Rizin
resources.desc: Reverse-engineering framework with command-line analysis and reusable libraries.

resources.name: Rubber Room
resources.desc: Browser PE workbench with x86-64 disassembly, partial Win32 API emulation and experimental C-like pseudocode that may omit program logic; alpha.

resources.name: GDB
resources.desc: Native debugger with scripting and remote-debugging support.

resources.name: GEF
resources.desc: Single-file GDB extension that adds context views, heap inspection, and commands for exploit development and binary analysis.

resources.name: LLDB
resources.desc: LLVM debugger for native programs, including macOS and iOS development workflows.

resources.name: pwndbg
resources.desc: Debugger extensions for inspecting memory, assembly, and runtime state during binary analysis.

resources.name: rr
resources.desc: Records and replays Linux process execution for repeatable debugging.

resources.name: WinDbg
resources.desc: Microsoft debugger for Windows user-mode and kernel debugging, crash dump analysis, and Time Travel Debugging; version 1.2610.1001.0 and later include the official WinDbg MCP server.

resources.name: x64dbg
resources.desc: Windows user-mode debugger for inspecting native executables and libraries.

resources.name: bpftrace
resources.desc: Linux eBPF tracing language for observing kernel and user-space functions; available probes and permissions depend on the host kernel.

resources.name: DynamoRIO
resources.desc: Dynamic binary instrumentation platform for building tools that observe or modify instructions at runtime, with bundled tracing and memory-checking tools.

resources.name: Frida
resources.desc: Injects scripts into running processes to trace calls, inspect data, and change behavior.

resources.name: Intel Pin
resources.desc: Dynamic binary instrumentation framework for writing analysis tools for x86 and x86-64 programs on Linux and Windows; closed source, free for any use.

resources.name: QBDI
resources.desc: LLVM-based dynamic binary instrumentation framework for x86, x86-64, ARM, and AArch64, with C, C++, and Python APIs and Frida integration.

resources.name: r2frida
resources.desc: radare2 plugin for Frida-backed process inspection and instrumentation; requires a compatible radare2 build and a working Frida session with the target.

resources.name: strace
resources.desc: Linux system-call tracer for inspecting process I/O, signals, syscall arguments, and return values.

resources.name: Sysinternals Suite
resources.desc: Microsoft utilities, including Process Monitor, Process Explorer, and Autoruns, for observing process, file, registry, and network activity on Windows.

resources.name: System Informer
resources.desc: Windows 10+ process and system inspector for handles, memory, services, and related kernel information; some views require elevated access.

resources.name: TinyTracer
resources.desc: Intel Pin tool for tracing execution and selected function or API calls; use the documented platform build and a matching Pin kit.

resources.name: uftrace
resources.desc: Linux function-call tracer for C/C++, Rust, and Python, with call graphs and timing data; native-code coverage depends on instrumentation or supported dynamic tracing.

resources.name: Al-Khaser
resources.desc: Windows proof-of-concept suite for exercising anti-debugging, anti-VM, anti-hooking, and other analysis-environment checks.

resources.name: de4dot
resources.desc: .NET deobfuscator and unpacker for assemblies protected by common obfuscators; archived in 2020 and no longer updated.

resources.name: HollowsHunter
resources.desc: Windows process scanner using PE-sieve to find and dump injected or modified code across running processes; findings require manual investigation.

resources.name: PE-sieve
resources.desc: Scans a running process for injected or modified code, such as hollowed modules, hooks, and shellcode, and dumps what it finds.

resources.name: Scylla
resources.desc: Windows x86/x64 import-table reconstruction tool for dumped PE files; upstream documents older Windows versions, so current-host compatibility needs checking.

resources.name: ScyllaHide
resources.desc: Windows x86/x64 user-mode anti-anti-debugging library with x64dbg, OllyDbg, and IDA integrations; debugger and plugin versions must match.

resources.name: CAPE Sandbox
resources.desc: Automated sandbox derived from Cuckoo that runs samples in virtual machines and records behavior, unpacked payloads, and malware configurations.

resources.name: Didier Stevens Suite
resources.desc: Python utilities for inspecting PDF, OLE, scripts, and other suspicious document inputs; dependencies and input support vary by script.

resources.name: Dumpulator
resources.desc: Emulates selected user-mode code from Windows minidumps for tasks such as string decryption and unpacking; dump completeness and supported execution context limit what can run.

resources.name: FakeNet-NG
resources.desc: Intercepts traffic and emulates network services for dynamic analysis; supports Windows and selected Linux modes, with platform-specific setup and traffic-redirection privileges.

resources.name: FLARE-VM
resources.desc: Installation scripts that turn a Windows virtual machine into a malware-analysis and reverse-engineering workstation.

resources.name: Malduck
resources.desc: Python library of cryptography, compression, and memory-model helpers with a YARA-driven framework for writing your own malware configuration extractors; it does not ship family extractors.

resources.name: MemProcFS
resources.desc: Exposes memory dumps and live memory as a virtual file system and Python, C, and Rust APIs, with process and forensic views for Windows targets; mounting requires Dokany, FUSE, or macFUSE.

resources.name: mwemu
resources.desc: Emulates x86/x64 and AArch64 code for PE, ELF, and Mach-O investigations, with Windows API models and kernel-driver memory-lifetime checks; Windows-focused, with growing Linux/macOS support and Rust 1.95+ required to build the reviewed source.

resources.name: oletools
resources.desc: Python tools for inspecting Office, OLE, and RTF files and extracting macros, embedded objects, and other document artifacts.

resources.name: REMnux
resources.desc: Linux toolkit for analyzing malicious executables, documents, scripts, and network traffic, available as a virtual machine, container, or installer.

resources.name: Speakeasy
resources.desc: Windows emulation framework for PE files, drivers, and shellcode that produces API reports within a modeled runtime.

resources.name: Volatility 3
resources.desc: Memory forensics framework for extracting processes, modules, network connections, and other artifacts from memory images.

resources.name: YARA
resources.desc: Identifies and classifies files with rules over strings, byte patterns, and file properties; in maintenance mode, with YARA-X as its successor.

resources.name: YARA-X
resources.desc: Rust-based rule-scanning engine with CLI and language bindings; check its documented differences before migrating YARA rules.

resources.name: Androguard
resources.desc: Python tooling for analyzing Android applications, bytecode, and call relationships.

resources.name: Apktool
resources.desc: Decodes Android resources and Smali code, and rebuilds APKs after edits.

resources.name: AsmResolver
resources.desc: Library for reading, modifying, and rebuilding native and managed PE files, including .NET metadata and application bundles.

resources.name: CFR
resources.desc: Java class and JAR decompiler for inspecting managed code; requires a Java runtime, and language-feature compatibility varies by input and release.

resources.name: dnSpyEx
resources.desc: .NET debugger and assembly editor maintained as a continuation of dnSpy.

resources.name: ILSpy
resources.desc: .NET assembly browser and decompiler with GUI and command-line interfaces.

resources.name: JADX
resources.desc: Android DEX decompiler with code navigation and search in a graphical interface or CLI.

resources.name: JEB
resources.desc: Android decompiler and analysis platform with edition-dependent native analysis and official MCP capabilities that vary by version; commercial.

resources.name: Medusa
resources.desc: Frida-based modular mobile runtime-analysis framework; documented hosts are Linux and macOS, with limited Windows functionality and target-side instrumentation prerequisites.

resources.name: MobSF
resources.desc: Automated static and dynamic analysis of Android, iOS, and Windows mobile apps, with a web interface and REST API.

resources.name: OWASP MASTG
resources.desc: Mobile security testing guidance with Android and iOS reverse-engineering techniques.

resources.name: Recaf
resources.desc: Java bytecode analysis and editing environment.

resources.name: Vineflower
resources.desc: Java decompiler focused on modern language features and readable output; requires Java 17 or newer to run current releases.

resources.name: class-dump
resources.desc: Generates Objective-C headers from Mach-O binaries; unmaintained since 2019 and without Swift support, so ipsw class-dump is a maintained alternative.

resources.name: Hopper
resources.desc: macOS disassembler and decompiler with Objective-C and Swift support, LLDB and GDB debugging, and scripting. Commercial, with a free demo.

resources.name: ipsw
resources.desc: Command-line toolkit for downloading and examining iOS and macOS firmware, dyld shared caches, kernelcaches, and Mach-O binaries.

resources.name: LLDB scripts by Derek Selander
resources.desc: LLDB commands, aliases, and Python helpers for Apple-platform investigations; individual scripts have architecture and debugger-version limits.

resources.name: objection
resources.desc: Frida-based toolkit for exploring iOS and Android apps at runtime, including class inspection, method hooking, and certificate-pinning bypass.

resources.name: pymobiledevice3
resources.desc: CLI and Python API for iOS device services, including logs, crash reports, packet capture, and developer tooling with version-dependent tunnel requirements.

resources.name: Blutter
resources.desc: Flutter AOT analysis tool for recent Android arm64 libapp.so files, producing annotated assembly, object-pool dumps, and Frida templates.

resources.name: GoReSym
resources.desc: Recovers function names, types, and build metadata from Go binaries, including stripped ones.

resources.name: Heimdall
resources.desc: EVM bytecode-analysis toolkit for disassembly, decompilation, and contract inspection; inferred source, types, and signatures require validation.

resources.name: hermes-dec
resources.desc: Parses, disassembles, and decompiles React Native Hermes bytecode into register-based pseudo-code with incomplete JavaScript semantics; HBC 98 and 99 load with an unsupported-version warning.

resources.name: Hermit
resources.desc: Interactive toolkit for inspecting, disassembling, decompiling, and structurally patching React Native Hermes bytecode; supports HBC 94, 95, and 96, with HBC 98 unsupported.

resources.name: pycdc
resources.desc: Disassembles and decompiles Python bytecode from .pyc files; decompilation of recent Python versions can be incomplete.

resources.name: pyinstxtractor
resources.desc: Extracts the contents of PyInstaller executables, including the bytecode needed for decompilation; the pyinstxtractor-ng fork uses xdis so the host Python need not match the build version and supports PyInstaller archive decryption when the embedded key can be recovered, but neither tool decompiles bytecode.

resources.name: PyLingual
resources.desc: Model-assisted CPython 3.6+ bytecode decompiler that recompiles its output and flags mismatched code objects for manual review; requires Python 3.12+ to run and downloads large per-version models.

resources.name: r2flutter
resources.desc: radare2 plugin and CLI for recovering Dart AOT snapshot metadata from Flutter binaries; requires radare2 6.2.2+, primarily targets AArch64, and depends on snapshot layout.

resources.name: Redress
resources.desc: Recovers compiler metadata, packages, types, and symbols from stripped Go executables; target Go-version compatibility depends on the selected release and GoRE parser.

resources.name: reFlutter
resources.desc: Flutter mobile-analysis framework that instruments matching engine builds and produces method or type information; Android/iOS architecture and engine-version support varies.

resources.name: WhatsABI
resources.desc: TypeScript library for inferring Ethereum ABI entries and resolving proxy metadata from bytecode; inferred signatures and types are not original-source recovery.

resources.name: boofuzz
resources.desc: Python framework for describing a protocol's message fields and sending mutated messages to a target, useful for testing a reconstructed protocol against a live service; crash detection needs a process monitor or restart callback.

resources.name: Burp Suite
resources.desc: Intercepting proxy and toolkit for inspecting, replaying, and modifying HTTP and WebSocket traffic. Commercial, with a free Community Edition.

resources.name: Chrome DevTools
resources.desc: Browser tools for stepping through JavaScript, inspecting network requests, and examining runtime state.

resources.name: HTTP Toolkit
resources.desc: Intercepts and inspects HTTP(S) traffic from browsers, desktop applications, Android devices, and containers with automated interception setup. Commercial, with a free open-source edition.

resources.name: mitmproxy
resources.desc: Intercepts, inspects, and modifies HTTP traffic with interactive tools and Python scripts.

resources.name: Netzob
resources.desc: Python protocol-inference library for exploring fields, messages, and state models from captures; installation needs native dependencies and the documented Python environment.

resources.name: Protobuf Decoder
resources.desc: Web application that decodes Protobuf messages without a schema and shows field numbers, wire types, and possible value interpretations.

resources.name: Scapy
resources.desc: Python packet framework for dissecting and constructing protocols, reading PCAPs, and scripting network experiments.

resources.name: WABT
resources.desc: WebAssembly utilities for converting, inspecting, validating, and decompiling modules.

resources.name: wasm-tools
resources.desc: Bytecode Alliance tools for inspecting, validating, and transforming WebAssembly modules, components, and WIT interfaces.

resources.name: webcrack
resources.desc: Deobfuscates JavaScript and unpacks common bundler output to make code easier to inspect.

resources.name: Wireshark
resources.desc: Captures and dissects network traffic for protocol investigation.

resources.name: avatar2
resources.desc: Coordinates debuggers, emulators, and physical targets for embedded analysis; each endpoint needs its own compatible backend and any associated hardware.

resources.name: Binwalk
resources.desc: Identifies embedded files and extracts content from firmware images.

resources.name: ChipWhisperer
resources.desc: Hardware and Python tooling for side-channel power analysis and fault-injection experiments; live capture and glitching require compatible capture and target hardware.

resources.name: EMBA
resources.desc: Firmware security analyzer that extracts images, runs static and emulation-based checks, and produces reports and SBOMs.

resources.name: esptool
resources.desc: Serial bootloader utility for reading or flashing Espressif devices, with offline image-info inspection of firmware headers, segments, checksums, and SHA-256 hashes; requires Python 3.10+, and 5.6.0 returns exit code 0 for checksum/hash mismatches.

resources.name: Facedancer
resources.desc: Python USB device-emulation and proxy framework for compatible hardware on GNU/Linux; 3.x does not support legacy scripts and backend capabilities vary.

resources.name: FACT
resources.desc: Linux firmware extraction, analysis, and comparison platform; the native installer has specific distribution and Python requirements, while the separate Docker route is unmaintained.

resources.name: FirmAE
resources.desc: Emulates Linux-based router and IP camera firmware for dynamic analysis, using heuristics that make full-system emulation succeed more often.

resources.name: flashrom
resources.desc: Reads, writes, and verifies flash chips through supported programmers, for dumping or restoring firmware from hardware.

resources.name: Glasgow Interface Explorer
resources.desc: Programmable hardware interface explorer with applets for probing and interacting with digital buses; requires Glasgow hardware.

resources.name: HALucinator
resources.desc: Firmware-rehosting framework that replaces selected hardware-abstraction-layer calls with models; requires its emulation toolchain and target-specific handlers or configuration.

resources.name: OFRAK
resources.desc: Framework for unpacking, analyzing, modifying, and repacking binary artifacts.

resources.name: OpenOCD
resources.desc: Connects to hardware debug interfaces for on-chip debugging and flash access.

resources.name: Packetry
resources.desc: USB 2.0 protocol analyzer for Cynthion captures and offline PCAP files using the LINKTYPE_USB_2_0 format.

resources.name: Proxmark3
resources.desc: RFID and NFC research client and firmware for compatible Proxmark3 hardware; client, firmware, and device variants need to match.

resources.name: QEMU
resources.desc: Machine emulator for running firmware and programs built for other architectures, with a GDB stub for debugging.

resources.name: Renode
resources.desc: Embedded-system simulator with scriptable platform and peripheral models for repeatable firmware debugging and observation.

resources.name: ripcord
resources.desc: Ghidra-based firmware-analysis pipeline producing queryable Parquet tables for DuckDB; requires Ghidra 11.2+ with PyGhidra and Python 3.11+, with optional simulation tooling.

resources.name: sigrok
resources.desc: Signal analysis tools and protocol decoders for logic analyzers and related hardware.

resources.name: UEFITool
resources.desc: Parses UEFI firmware structures and extracts or replaces modules.

resources.name: unblob
resources.desc: Extracts nested archives, compressed data, and filesystem images from firmware and other files.

resources.name: usb-rea
resources.desc: Infers USB protocol fields, counters, checksums, and multi-packet commands from captures of labelled actions, with frame-number evidence, and generates pyusb driver code and Wireshark Lua dissectors; requires Python 3.10+, with usbmon plus dumpcap/tshark on Linux or USBPcap on Windows for capture, and remains alpha without physical-device validation.

resources.name: 010 Editor
resources.desc: Hex editor with binary templates for inspecting structured files. Commercial.

resources.name: Construct
resources.desc: Declarative Python library for parsing and building binary formats with composable schemas and validation.

resources.name: CyberChef
resources.desc: Browser-based workbench for decoding, decompressing, and transforming data with exportable recipes.

resources.name: Hex Fiend
resources.desc: macOS hex editor for inspecting and editing large binary files, with binary templates and an embeddable framework.

resources.name: Hex Harbinger
resources.desc: Browser hex editor that overlays structure templates for PE, ELF, Mach-O and ZIP files and highlights the parsed fields; alpha.

resources.name: ImHex
resources.desc: Hex editor with a pattern language for describing and exploring binary structures.

resources.name: Kaitai Struct
resources.desc: Describes binary formats declaratively and generates parsers in multiple languages.

resources.name: Struct Smith
resources.desc: Browser editor for Spec binary-format schemas, with a live parse tree, byte highlighting and diagnostics; alpha, with a 64 MiB input limit.

resources.name: AssetRipper
resources.desc: Unity asset-analysis and export tool with version-dependent support and additional paid Premium features.

resources.name: Cheat Engine
resources.desc: Memory scanner, debugger, and disassembler for finding and changing values in running processes, mainly used for game and application modding.

resources.name: Cpp2IL
resources.desc: Recovers types, methods, and IL from Unity IL2CPP builds into .NET assemblies and other outputs; described by its author as work in progress.

resources.name: FModel
resources.desc: Windows x64 GUI for inspecting and extracting Unreal Engine game archives and assets; title-specific mappings, versions, or encryption keys may be needed.

resources.name: GDRE Tools
resources.desc: Recovers Godot projects from exported games, including PCK extraction, GDScript decompilation, and resource conversion.

resources.name: Il2CppDumper
resources.desc: Restores Unity IL2CPP type and method metadata for use in IDA, Ghidra, and other tools; no commits since July 2024, with Cpp2IL as a maintained alternative.

resources.name: ReClass.NET
resources.desc: Interactive process-memory structure editor for Windows and Linux; upstream documents Linux support tested on Ubuntu 18.04, rather than current-distribution validation.

resources.name: Source 2 Viewer
resources.desc: Parser, decompiler, exporter, and Windows viewer for Valve Source 2 resources and VPK archives; format coverage and export fidelity vary by resource type.

resources.name: UModel
resources.desc: Unreal Engine package viewer and asset exporter for Windows and Linux; game/version compatibility varies, and the official site leaves licensing undetermined.

resources.name: vgmstream
resources.desc: Library and command-line tools for decoding proprietary game-audio streams; supported formats, codec dependencies, and player integrations vary.

resources.name: BinDiff
resources.desc: Compares disassembled binaries to identify similar functions and changes between builds; inputs come from the BinExport exporters for IDA Pro, Ghidra, and Binary Ninja; the current IDA plugin source requires IDA Pro 9.4+, while the 2024 release documents IDA SDK 8.0+ for building that plugin.

resources.name: Binlex
resources.desc: Binary-feature analysis framework with CLI and language bindings for similarity and corpus investigation; build and plugin dependencies vary by interface.

resources.name: Diaphora
resources.desc: Binary diffing plugin for comparing functions and transferring analysis in IDA.

resources.name: ghidriff
resources.desc: Ghidra-based command-line binary diffing engine with JSON, Markdown, and optional HTML reports; requires compatible Ghidra, PyGhidra, and JDK versions.

resources.name: angr
resources.desc: Python framework for symbolic execution and program analysis; angr-management is its official GUI front end, not a separate analysis engine.

resources.name: BINSEC
resources.desc: Binary-analysis platform combining symbolic execution, abstract interpretation, and SMT solving; source builds require OCaml and compatible solver/backend dependencies.

resources.name: flare-emu
resources.desc: Archived Unicorn-based emulation helper for IDA Pro, Rizin, and radare2 scripting; analysis-host APIs and Python bindings must match the archived source.

resources.name: KLEE
resources.desc: LLVM-bitcode symbolic-execution engine for generating test inputs and finding assertion violations; requires a compatible compiler/runtime setup and does not imply proof from an incomplete run.

resources.name: Miasm
resources.desc: Python reverse-engineering framework with an intermediate representation, emulation, symbolic execution, and assemblers and disassemblers for several architectures.

resources.name: PANDA
resources.desc: QEMU-based whole-system record/replay and analysis framework with taint-analysis plugins; analysis depends on supported guest architectures, recordings, and matching plugins.

resources.name: Qiling
resources.desc: Emulates binaries with operating-system services for scripted runtime analysis.

resources.name: S2E
resources.desc: Selective symbolic-execution platform for analyzing programs across OS boundaries; requires a supported Linux host, the S2E toolchain, and prepared guest images.

resources.name: Triton
resources.desc: Dynamic binary analysis library with symbolic execution, taint analysis, and AST representations of instruction semantics, usable from C++ or Python.

resources.name: Unicorn
resources.desc: CPU emulation library for executing and instrumenting machine code across architectures.

resources.name: Z3
resources.desc: SMT solver with command-line and language APIs for expressing and solving analysis constraints; satisfiability results depend on the model and solver outcome, including possible unknown results.

resources.name: BAP
resources.desc: Binary-analysis platform for lifting native code into an intermediate language and running analyses; source installation uses OCaml/opam and a compatible LLVM toolchain.

resources.name: Capstone
resources.desc: Multi-architecture disassembly library for building analysis tools.

resources.name: Keystone
resources.desc: Multi-architecture assembler library, the counterpart to Capstone, for turning assembly text into machine code when patching binaries or building test inputs; GPL-2.0 with a separate commercial license, and the latest PyPI release (0.9.2, 2020) ships wheels only for x86 and x86-64 hosts.

resources.name: Remill
resources.desc: Library for lifting supported machine instructions into LLVM bitcode; requires compatible LLVM and build dependencies, with Windows support documented as experimental.

resources.name: Zydis
resources.desc: x86/x86-64 instruction decoding and encoding library for building analysis tools; source builds use CMake or the documented Visual Studio project.

resources.name: Binary Ninja MCP Server
resources.desc: Built-in Binary Ninja server that exposes functions, symbols, strings, disassembly, IL, and decompiled code to MCP clients; the headless variant requires a Commercial or Ultimate license.

resources.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
resources.desc: Official MCP server for inspecting Chrome network activity, runtime state, console output, and performance traces; requires Node.js LTS and Chrome.

resources.name: Dex Explore by Exmergo
resources.desc: Read-only database-exploration skill that profiles columns, infers candidate keys and row grain, and probes candidate joins; PII flags are heuristic, and execution requires uv and Python 3.11+.

resources.name: Gepetto
resources.desc: IDA plugin that asks language models to explain decompiled functions and rename their variables; requires IDA 7.6 or later and access to a supported model provider.

resources.name: Ghidra MCP Server
resources.desc: Connects AI clients to Ghidra analysis through MCP.

resources.name: GhidraMCP
resources.desc: Ghidra plugin and MCP server for decompiling, listing, and renaming functions and data; the original project from which Ghidra MCP Server was derived.

resources.name: Hex-Rays IDA MCP
resources.desc: Official IDA MCP server for agent access to binary analysis; requires IDA 9.4+ with idalib, Python 3.11+, and uv, with IDA licensing separate from the server.

resources.name: IDA Pro MCP
resources.desc: Exposes IDA analysis and scripting capabilities to MCP clients; requires a compatible IDA installation.

resources.name: JADX-AI-MCP
resources.desc: Connects AI clients to JADX for Android application analysis.

resources.name: OpenDeviceDB
resources.desc: Experimental device-support registry with an MCP server for finding upstream protocol and firmware projects by model, FCC ID, or USB vid:pid; the npm server requires Node.js 20+, imported record quality varies, and claims/findings require a local checkout and pull request for public inclusion.

resources.name: radare2 MCP
resources.desc: Provides an MCP interface to radare2 for agent-driven binary analysis.

resources.name: re-audit
resources.desc: Statically audits ELF/PE/Mach-O binaries and Android APKs for missing exploit mitigations (NX, PIE/ASLR, RELRO, stack canary), hardcoded secrets, and risky exported components; runs as a CLI or MCP server with no network access and no execution of the target. Findings are heuristic candidates for manual review, not confirmed vulnerabilities. Requires Python 3.10+.
